comparison: Perfect agreement on method development claims (C5, C26-C36). Both evaluations find the enrichment methodology well-validated and supported. OpenEval emphasizes RT-qPCR validation and sequencing metrics; peer reviewers explicitly affirm the methodological advance with all three reviewers praising the technical achievement.

Perfect agreement on RNA-seq differential expression findings (C6, C37-C40, C97-C98). Both evaluations support the transcriptomic analysis and acknowledge the longitudinal study as a significant contribution. OpenEval highlights statistical rigor; peer reviewers confirm the data demonstrate successful transcriptome sequencing.

Perfect agreement on validation against known regulatory programs (C41-C43, C99-C100). Both evaluations accept the concordance with RpoS, Rrp1, and RelBbu targets as internal validation. OpenEval notes appropriate interpretation of partial concordance; peer reviewers treat this as implicit validation without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on validation against prior studies (C44-C46, C101-C103), though peer result R4 also includes novel gene claims (C47, C76, C119). OpenEval finds partial concordance appropriately interpreted; peer reviewers accept both the comparisons and novel gene discoveries without challenge, noting manuscript improvements.

Both address novel gene identification (C47, C76, C119-C120). OpenEval emphasizes systematic comparison and functional categorization; peer reviewers accept the 26 novel genes as legitimate discoveries and acknowledge the value of the ex vivo approach.

Perfect agreement on genomic distribution findings (C48-C50, C61-C62). Both evaluations accept the plasmid vs. chromosome localization patterns as consistent with established Bb genome organization. This descriptive finding is uncontested by both evaluations.

Strong agreement on prophage-related findings (C63-C67, C104-C105), though OpenEval also includes transmission gene claims (C51-C52). Both evaluations accept prophage upregulation data; OpenEval notes speculation about prophage induction is appropriately qualified; peer reviewers treat this as legitimate novel observation.

Strong agreement on outer surface protein changes (C7-C8, C53-C54, C68-C71, C77-C78, C120). Both evaluations support extensive outer surface remodeling as a key finding. OpenEval emphasizes functional categorization; peer reviewers note minor concern about incomplete analysis of downregulated genes but accept the core findings.

Agreement on mass spectrometry findings (C55-C58, C83). Both evaluations accept the proteomic data and identification of candidate tick-Bb interaction proteins. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate controls; peer reviewers acknowledge this as valuable preliminary work, noting it remains descriptive without follow-up experiments.

Both address tick protein analysis (C59-C60, C111, C113-C114). OpenEval supports functional enrichment findings and notes speculation is appropriately qualified; peer reviewers accept the mass spectrometry approach as useful for identifying interaction candidates, though note lack of experimental follow-up.

Significant disagreement on methodological limitations (C85-C88, C124-C125). OpenEval finds limitations appropriately acknowledged with supporting data; peer reviewers express uncertainty, explicitly requesting additional data on sensitivity, limit of detection, and method boundaries. Reviewers indicate insufficient characterization of potential biases.

Agreement on study contributions and value (C75, C82, C129-C130). Both evaluations affirm the resource and methodological value. OpenEval notes appropriate speculation about future applications; all three peer reviewers explicitly confirm the work's importance and utility for the field.

Agreement on bulk RNA-seq limitations (C89-C91). Both evaluations accept caveats about population-level analysis and single-cell heterogeneity. OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment with supporting citations; peer reviewers explicitly recognize the descriptive nature and accept the limitation discussion as appropriate contextualization.

OpenEval evaluates background and rationale claims (C1-C3, C10-C25) as well-supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviews typically focus on novel findings rather than background literature.

OpenEval evaluates synthesis and discussion claims (C72-C73, C79-C81, C84, C108-C110, C115-C117, C123) as appropriately supported with qualified speculation. No direct peer review correspondence, though peer result R10 touches on C108 regarding future applications.

OpenEval evaluates technical sequencing details and quality control (C92-C96) as appropriately documented, including P. fulva contamination detection. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these technical specifications.
